rationale: Client4.ExecuteCommand/ExecuteCommandWithTeam decode server-emitted responses through the same CommandResponseFromJSON that now hard-fails on IsValid, while plugin/built-in responses (app/command.go:234-252) never pass through it server-side; the remedy is the same as thread 6's ask (move the call to the two ingest call sites), though the rationale differs.
No test case puts a null element in extra_responses, so the nil-continue branch of IsValid is untested; correct but a small coverage nit.

len(o.Text) counts bytes against a fixed 65535 whereas Post.IsValid enforces utf8.RuneCountInString against a configurable rune limit (PostMessageMaxRunesV2 or column/4), so the two limits diverge in both directions; this is the byte-vs-character defect thread 0 raises.
The comment restates the next line; purely stylistic.
A considered-and-cleared note asserting no defect.
65535 is a local literal while PostMessageMaxBytesV2 = 65535 already exists in the same package and the file declares its other constants at package level; correct, small.
The only two in_channel rows in the table both expect errors, so the accept path for in_channel is unpinned; a fair but small test gap.
Cleared note; the *AppError is nil-tested before it is returned as error, so no typed-nil escape.
TestCommandResponseFromHTTPBody is unchanged and has no case pinning whether text/plain bodies are subject to the new validation; a small, actionable test observation.

IsValid checks only response_type, text length and recursion; attachments (which already have MessageAttachment.IsValid), URLs, Type, etc. are untouched, so 'strict validation' overstates the scope. Correct but mostly a framing/scope comment.
Only the 65536 rejection is tested; nothing pins that 65535 is accepted, so a > to >= regression would pass. Small test-boundary nit.

IsValid explicitly skips nil ExtraResponses entries, and HandleCommandResponse passes each entry to HandleCommandResponsePost which dereferences response.Type unguarded, so {"extra_responses":[null]} from a command webhook or custom command reaches a nil-pointer panic; pre-existing, but the new validator lets a known-crashing shape through.
IsValid is fully exercised through the CommandResponseFromJSON table with the same inputs a direct test would use; a direct test is a preference, not a gap.
On io.ReadAll failure the function returns (nil, nil), discarding the error; both callers cope via a nil check but the read error is lost. Pre-existing and small.
Cleared note asserting no defect.
The nested error is returned verbatim with no index, unlike Post.IsValid which prefixes the attachment index; a small debuggability nit.

One invalid nested entry makes the whole decode fail and discards the main message, whereas HandleCommandResponse tolerates per-entry failures; this is the hard-error-instead-of-warning defect thread 4 raises, viewed through the nested case.
Cleared note asserting no defect.
The asymmetry is real, but no consumer reads ExtraResponses below the first level (app/command.go:621-628), so nested-nested attachments being unstringified has no effect.
DetailedError omits the offending value and actual/max length while Post.IsValid reports Length/MaxLength; a small actionable debuggability nit.
Cleared note asserting no defect.

commandWebhook's r.Body is already wrapped in http.MaxBytesReader (ServiceSettings.MaximumPayloadSizeBytes, default 300000) by the generic handler, so the implied unbounded read does not exist; also pre-existing and outside the diff.

Adding IsValid to the decoder turns previously tolerated payloads (unknown response_type, long text) into a whole-command failure at both ingest sites with no gate; this is exactly thread 4's 'hard error might break existing servers, log a warning instead'.
Blank-line spacing; purely stylistic.

True that i18n-check runs clean-empty/check-empty-src rather than 'i18n check', but this is a pre-existing repo tooling gap outside the PR's scope; the actionable point for this PR is the missing keys themselves (thread 1).

CommandResponseFromHTTPBody only routes application/json through CommandResponseFromJSON; text/plain goes to CommandResponseFromPlainText with no IsValid, so the same oversized text is rejected or accepted depending solely on Content-Type. Real inconsistency in the new validation, not raised by any thread.
Asserts no defect.
Cleared note asserting no defect.
Whitespace inside a raw JSON string literal; purely stylistic.
Notes idiomatic shadowing and asserts no defect.
grep of server/i18n/en.json finds neither new ID, so translation falls back to the raw key; this is what thread 1 asks to fix via make i18n-extract.
Pre-existing table convention; the summary itself asserts no defect.

The ShouldError branch checks only assert.Error/assert.Nil, so the new cases (especially the multi-line extra_responses JSON) would still pass if they failed on a JSON syntax error rather than validation; asserting the AppError Id would pin the intent. Correct, small.
DoCommandRequest wraps the decode error in a fresh 500 AppError and commandWebhook in a fresh hardcoded 400, so the StatusBadRequest set in IsValid is never what the caller sees; true and minor.
Most IsValid methods in server/public/model (roughly 59 of 69) have no doc comment, so this matches package convention; a preference.
